result.title: Machina Pauliana: A neuro-symbolic approach to the actio pauliana in Dutch insolvency law
result.summary: Applying a legal provision frequently requires both structured rule-based reasoning and sensitivity to open-textured terms developed in case law. The actio pauliana of Article 42 of the Dutch Bankruptcy Act (Faillissementswet, Fw), which allows an insolvency practitioner to avoid transactions that prejudice creditors, requires both. We present a neuro-symbolic model of Article 42 Fw. Its symbolic core is written in Catala in a literate style that keeps statute and formalisation aligned and was developed through pair programming, with open-textured terms represented as boolean inputs where neural components couple to the symbolic solver. A neural routine structures a case's natural-language facts into boolean and date inputs. Neural subroutines resolve the open-textured terms through case-based reasoning over Dutch civil judgments, retrieved through a pipeline that filters on the requirement being resolved and expands along the procedural chain of a case. Segmenting and labelling those judgments attains high precision and recall against a manually annotated gold standard of 100 judgments. On ten hand-annotated cases the neuro-symbolic model handles most criteria reasonably but struggles with the knowledge requirement. Retrieval depth shows no clear quantitative effect, although retrieved judgments provide explicit grounding in prior case law.

AI.brief_summary: 该文为荷兰破产法第42条构建神经符号模型：以 Catala 编写的符号核心对应法条，由神经模块把自然语言案情转为布尔与日期输入、并通过对荷兰民事判决的检索与类案推理消解开放文本要件，检索流水线成效以人工标注判决集评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 属较远的法律推理领域，但其「神经模块只负责消解开放要件、其余交由符号求解」的分工，以及检索深度对结果无明显影响的观察，可能为 LVR 中证据筛选与贡献分配、检索量是否真正进入推理状态提供可核查的类比线索。
